chapter: Vidals, blues, teachers and the Silver Leaf band
title: White bands and players start playing jazz around 1915; their teachers
summary: Charles names Schilling, Vega, Fisher and Brown, and says the white boys studied with Perez and Monette.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Did you ever know George Schilling, Happy Schilling? Yeah. The white trombone player? He had a band, he called it Schilling's Black and White Band. Half white and half colored. They had plenty of bands. They used to play a lot of white bands then. Yeah.
Well now was this one of the earlier bands?
Yeah, that was around what, 1916 or so?
He was a hit. He was going big then.
Well we didn't ask him about that, about when the white players began to play. What time did those white players begin to show up in the bands in New Orleans?

Playing jazz? Oh I'm sure it must have been around 1915 and 16. Because Vega and them, they the first ones started. Lawrence Vega, you heard of them? Yeah. Well Lawrence Vega and them, they the first ones start playing that jazz. They were. And not Johnny Deechard because Johnny Deechard was in the theater. Oh my. Let me see what's the other name. Schilling, Vega, and they had another one there.
There was Fisher and Brown. Fisher and Brown.
That's right. And Jack Lane had a band. Well that was on, he came after, but those fellas they started doing, a little after I did.
That's right. Well now whom did they work and study with down there, the same men that you had?
No, they had their own band, those white boys. They had their own band. None of them did.

Oh, Manuel Parade, the one who started Vega, Lawrence Vega. Yeah. That's right. I don't know who started, Brown or them other fellas, but I know Lawrence Vega, he used to take music lessons the same time with me at Manuel. He did. That's right. But I didn't know him well, but I knew he was taking lessons with Manuel. Well, I took from Monetta.
Monetta had many white pupils, my teacher. Oh yes. All through the years. Oh yes.

Well over in life, he had over there for instance this very fine piano teacher that passed away some years ago, and she has a number of white students. This Romero girl had studied with her. Yeah, that makes sense.
